summary: Usharbudh Arya (1933–2015) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of London and held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1973.

Uta Reinöhl (born 1986) works in linguistics and Indology. She held a position at the University of Cologne in 2018 and was appointed Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken (born 1965) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at the University of Göttingen, she held posts at Göttingen, Heidelberg University, and the University of Oslo.

Ute Wallenböck works in Sinology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna and Sigmund Freud University Vienna, and has held posts at the University of Vienna, Palacký University Olomouc, Masaryk University, and the University of Bonn.

Uto von Melzer (1881–1961) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Graz (1919–1923), where he studied under Johann Kirste, Rudolf Meringer, and Hans Reichelt.

Utz Podzeit (1942–2022) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna. He held a post as Universitätsdozent at the University of Vienna starting in 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).
V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving as an editorial committee member (attested 2001) and supervisor/guide (attested 2026).

V. M. Subramanya Sharma is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as an assistant professor at Osmania University from 2011 to 2022 and joined the University of Delhi as an assistant professor in 2022.

Vinayaka P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist associated with the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he headed the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and served as Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).
V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who was attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught at Madras, served the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was adviser to the Adyar Library.

V. W. Paranjpe (1887–1976) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and was later Professor Emeritus at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading by 2017 and held a post there (attested 2018).

Vairamuthu Kanagaraj is an Indologist who studied at SASTRA and IIT Hyderabad. He worked as a Senior Research Fellow at NIIMH and Jayadev Memorial Rashtrotthana Hospital, and as a Teaching Assistant at IIT Hyderabad in 2026.

Valaiyattur Venkayya (1864–1912) was an epigraphist and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as acting Government Epigraphist of Madras and acting Government Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Harvard and Tokyo. He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and several universities in Japan, before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

Valentin Parisot (1800–1861) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics educated at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as professor of foreign literature at the University of Rennes, Grenoble Alpes University, and the University of Douai.

Valentin Trapp (1908–1993) was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich. He also studied at Visva-Bharati University and Banaras Hindu University under scholars including Hanns Oertel, Lucian Scherman, and Walther Wüst.

Valentina Stache-Rosen (1925–1980) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen and pursued further studies at SOAS University of London and Deccan College.

Valentine Ball (1843–1895) studied at Trinity College Dublin, later serving there as Professor of Geology and Mineralogy. He worked for the Geological Survey of India (1864–1881) and served as Director of the National Museum of Ireland (1883–1895).
